title: Exa 3.0 Workflow Setup for Agents, One Stage at a Time
summary: Exa 3.0 workflow runs authenticated searches returning page contents in one response. Set up your system, understand its limits, and fix common issues.
body_markdown:
## Which Exa plan fits you


Start on the Lite search type at **$4 per 1,000 requests** , and move up only when the results force you to, meaning you spend nothing on premium search power until you actually need it.


These rates come from[Usagepricing](https://www.usagepricing.com/blueprint/exa-ai) , checked 2026-11-12. They're per-request rates, not seat plans, so every monthly figure below is request volume multiplied by rate.


### Which Exa plan for solo testing


At $4 per 1,000 requests, a solo builder running 1,000 test searches in a month pays $4 on Lite, making early experimentation financially negligible.


Lite is the cheapest type, not the most capable. That is the catch. If your results come back thin, Fast and Auto both cost $7 per 1,000, so the same 1,000 searches become $7.


> Lite is the cheapest type, not the most capable. That is the catch.


### Which Exa plan for a team of five


If five people run 1,000 searches each, that makes 5,000 requests a month. On Lite that's $20, and on Auto at $7 per 1,000 it's $35.


The $15 gap is small, which means the choice should follow result quality, not budget. Pick Auto if your team can't tolerate misses, and Lite if speed of iteration matters more.


### Team of 25 with SSO or admin needs


At 1,000 searches each, 25 people make 25,000 requests. That's $100 on Lite, $175 on Auto, or $300 on Deep at $12 per 1,000.


Settle SSO, admin controls and seat floors with Exa directly before you commit. The published per-request rates don't cover them, and the request cost won't be the part that changes your bill.


### Heavy API volume


**At 100,000 requests a month** , Lite costs $400, Fast or Auto cost $700, and Deep costs $1,200, turning the technical choice of search tier into one with genuine budget consequences.


At this volume a single search-type decision moves the bill by $800 a month, a difference that becomes nearly $10,000 annually if you select the wrong tier.


Run Lite as the default, send only the queries that need depth to Deep, and measure the split before you scale.


If 10% of 100,000 requests go to Deep, you pay $360 for those and $360 for the Lite remainder, $720 in total instead of $1,200.
